faqs.question: How much is a large pizza at Domino's in 2026?
faqs.answer: A Large (14") cheese pizza is typically around $11.99 and a Large pepperoni around $12.99 at carryout, though prices vary by location. Ordering through Mix & Match or the $6.99 Each deal is usually cheaper. Verify at official checkout.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest way to order Domino's?
faqs.answer: Carryout deals and the $6.99 Each promotion are consistently the cheapest routes. Mix & Match lets you combine two or more items at a fixed per-item price, and Domino's Rewards earns you a free pizza over time.

faqs.question: Are Domino's prices the same at every location?
faqs.answer: No. Domino's stores are individually franchised and set their own prices, so the same pizza can cost different amounts in different cities. Always confirm the final total at checkout.

faqs.question: Does Domino's still have the Mix & Match deal?
faqs.answer: Mix & Match has been Domino's flagship value deal for years and remains widely available. The exact per-item price changes periodically, so check the current offer on the official app.

faqs.question: How much is a medium 2-topping pizza at Domino's?
faqs.answer: A Medium (12") two-topping pizza is typically around $11.49 at menu price, but it's usually cheaper as the classic Mix & Match item. It's one of the most deal-friendly orders on the menu.

faqs.question: What is the most expensive item on the Domino's menu?
faqs.answer: The loaded specialty pizzas in Large size sit at the top, usually around $16.99–$17.99 at menu price. Even those drop to the per-item deal rate through Mix & Match, so you rarely need to pay full price.

faqs.question: Does Domino's have a cheap lunch option?
faqs.answer: Yes. Hot sandwiches around $6.99–$7.99, oven-baked pasta near $7.99, and boneless chicken from $8.99 all make solid single-person lunches, especially through a value deal.

faqs.question: How often do Domino's prices change?
faqs.answer: Core menu prices are fairly stable, but individual franchises adjust them and deals rotate regularly. We refresh these example prices monthly and always tell you to verify the live total at checkout.

content:
So, What Does Domino's Actually Cost in 2026?

Let's be honest about something first. There's no single, magic price list for Domino's, no matter how much we all wish there were. Every store is its own little business, franchised and priced by whoever runs it. That corner shop near you and the one three towns over can charge different amounts for the exact same Large pepperoni. Wild, right? It catches people off guard all the time — they see a price online, drive over, and the total's a couple dollars off from what they expected.

So treat every number on this page as a solid ballpark rather than gospel. I've built these figures from what stores commonly post, and I keep them current month to month. When it's time to actually pay, though, the checkout screen is the only price that counts. Fair enough? Good. Now let's walk the whole menu, category by category, with real example prices for each — and I'll flag where the value hides and where people quietly overspend without noticing.

Pizza: Where Most People Start

A build-your-own pizza gets priced two ways at once — the size you pick, and how many toppings you pile on. A Large cheese usually lands around $11.99, and each extra topping tacks on a buck-fifty to two-fifty or so. Nothing dramatic on its own, but it adds up fast if you go wild. I've watched people turn a twelve-dollar pizza into a twenty-dollar one just by saying yes to every topping the app cheerfully suggests. Every topping, sauce and cheese option is priced up in our Domino's toppings guide.

PizzaSmall (10")Medium (12")Large (14")
Cheese~$7.99~$9.99~$11.99
Pepperoni~$8.99~$10.99~$12.99
2-topping build~$9.49~$11.49~$13.49

Here's the part people forget: crust choice doesn't just change the taste, it changes the mood of the whole meal. Hand Tossed is the safe, pillowy default that pleases almost everyone. Handmade Pan is the indulgent one, buttery and thick, and it's the crust I reach for when I want pizza to feel like a treat. Crunchy Thin is for folks who think most pizza has too much bread — light, crisp, and it lets the toppings do the talking. Brooklyn Style goes big and foldable. And there's a Gluten Free option in a small size if wheat's off the table. For how the sizes stack up on value, the pizza sizes guide breaks it all down.

How Toppings Change the Math

Toppings are where two identical-looking orders end up costing wildly different amounts. A plain cheese and a five-topping monster are the same base pizza, just priced worlds apart. My honest advice? Pick two or three toppings you genuinely love rather than six you're lukewarm on. It tastes better and costs less — a rare combination. And if you're going heavy on toppings anyway, jump to a specialty pizza, because you'll usually pay less for the same load. More on that right now.

Specialty Pizzas Are Sneaky Good Value

Now here's the thing about the specialty pies. They come pre-loaded, so the sticker price looks higher — a Large usually sits between $15.99 and $17.99. That number scares people off. But here's what they miss: almost all of them qualify for Mix & Match. That means you can grab a fully loaded ExtravaganZZa or a Philly Cheese Steak for the same per-item price as a plain two-topping. Read that again. More toppings, same money. Ordering a specialty inside a deal is one of the easiest wins on the whole menu, and it's the move I make nine times out of ten.

Specialty PizzaLarge ExampleBest For
ExtravaganZZa~$16.99Meat lovers, big appetites
Philly Cheese Steak~$16.99No-pork, cheesesteak fans
Pacific Veggie~$16.99Vegetarians
MeatZZa~$16.99All-meat cravings

Which specialty should you pick? If you love meat, the MeatZZa and ExtravaganZZa are your lane. Vegetarian? The Pacific Veggie is genuinely good and doesn't feel like a compromise. Want something that breaks the tomato-sauce mold entirely? The Philly Cheese Steak skips red sauce for a cheese base and tastes more like a sandwich than a pizza — in the best possible way.

Pasta, Chicken and Sandwiches

People sleep on the non-pizza menu, and I get why — you go to Domino's for pizza. But they're missing out. Oven-baked pasta like Chicken Alfredo or Italian Sausage Marinara runs roughly $7.99 to $8.99 and travels surprisingly well. Boneless chicken and wings start near $8.99 and make a great add-on when a pizza alone won't quite cut it. And the hot sandwiches — the Italian, the Chicken Bacon Ranch — hover around $6.99 to $7.99 and are quietly one of the better lunch options nobody talks about. Our Domino's sides menu guide prices up the whole non-pizza lineup, tots and desserts included.

Sides, Sweets and Something to Drink

The sides are where the real bargains hide, and honestly where I do most of my damage. Stuffed Cheesy Bread, Parmesan Bread Bites, Garlic Bread Twists — most sit in the $6.99 to $7.99 range and drop even lower inside a deal. Stuffed Cheesy Bread in particular is the one I'd tell a first-timer to try before anything else. For dessert? The Chocolate Lava Crunch Cakes are the move, around $4.99, molten in the middle, and genuinely worth it. The Marbled Cookie Brownie is the shareable pick if there's a crowd. Round it out with a 2-liter of Coke and you've fed the whole table for less than you'd think.

The Golden Rule: Don't Pay Full Price

If you take one thing from this entire guide, take this. You should almost never pay menu price at Domino's. The Mix & Match deal and the $6.99 Each promo exist precisely so you don't have to. Build your order inside one of them from the very first click. Then add Domino's Rewards on top, because every qualifying order earns points toward a free pizza whether you use a deal or not. And if you can swing by and grab it yourself, carryout beats delivery every single time once the fee and tip land. The full step-by-step is in my money-saving guide, and browsing the live coupons page before you order takes ten seconds and pays for itself.

The Mistake I See Constantly

Want to know the most common way people overpay? They add items one at a time at full price instead of building the order around a deal, then wonder why the total quietly crept past thirty bucks. Two minutes of planning — deal first, carryout if you can, signed into rewards — routinely knocks a quarter to nearly half off the total. It's not a secret hack. It's just paying attention, which most of us don't do when we're hungry and rushing.

How to Build a Smart Full Order

Let me put it all together with a real example. Say you're feeding a family of four. Two large pizzas through Mix & Match, one order of Stuffed Cheesy Bread, and a 2-liter. Order it carryout, signed into rewards. That's a complete dinner with leftovers, at a price that doesn't sting, plus points banking toward your next free pizza. That's the whole game — deal, side, drink, carryout, rewards. Repeat it and you'll consistently pay less than the person next to you ordering the same food at full price.

One Honest Caveat

I check these prices against posted menus and refresh this page monthly, but Domino's can change a price or pull a deal whenever it feels like it. Nothing here is a promise. This is an independent, unofficial guide written by people who just really like ordering pizza well and can't stand watching folks overpay for it. For live prices, current deals, and to actually place your order, the official Domino's app is your friend. Use this page to plan smart, then let checkout confirm the details. That's the deal — you plan, they cook, everybody wins.

faqs.question: How much is a Domino's specialty pizza?
faqs.answer: At menu price expect roughly $15.99 to $16.99 for a medium and about $16.99 to $18.99 for a large, depending on the pizza and your store. But specialty pizzas are regularly included in Mix & Match style offers at around $9.99 each for a medium, which is where almost everyone should be buying them.

faqs.question: Which Domino's specialty pizza is the best?
faqs.answer: It depends what you're after. ExtravaganZZa is the most loaded, Ultimate Pepperoni is the safest crowd-pleaser, Pacific Veggie is the best non-meat option, Philly Cheese Steak is the most different from a normal pizza, and the newer Spicy Chicken Bacon Ranch is the pick if you want heat.

faqs.question: What is on Domino's ExtravaganZZa?
faqs.answer: Pepperoni, ham, Italian sausage, beef, onions, green peppers, mushrooms, black olives and extra cheese. It is the most heavily loaded pizza Domino's makes and, at roughly 370 calories a slice on a large, also the heaviest.

faqs.question: What is Domino's Spicy Chicken Bacon Ranch pizza?
faqs.answer: It is Domino's newest specialty pizza, launched in late 2025 alongside the brand's 'Treat Yo Self' campaign. It is built with grilled chicken breast, creamy ranch, smoked bacon, jalapeños, provolone and mozzarella, finished with a buffalo sauce drizzle.

faqs.question: Which Domino's specialty pizza has the fewest calories?
faqs.answer: Pacific Veggie and Spinach & Feta, both around 230 calories per large slice. That is roughly 140 calories a slice less than the ExtravaganZZa, which adds up to a big difference across a few slices.

faqs.question: Can you customize a Domino's specialty pizza?
faqs.answer: Yes. Start from the specialty recipe and then add or remove toppings, change the crust and adjust the cheese. Removing a topping usually doesn't lower the price, but adding one often raises it, so check the total before you pay.

faqs.question: Is a specialty pizza better value than building your own?
faqs.answer: At full menu price, a specialty pizza is usually the better deal because you'd pay per-topping to recreate it. Inside a deal it flips — a two-topping build-your-own is often cheaper than a specialty, unless the offer specifically includes specialty pizzas.

faqs.question: Are specialty pizzas included in Domino's deals?
faqs.answer: Often, but not always. Domino's has run medium specialty pizzas at around $9.99 through Mix & Match, while some promotions such as certain any-crust offers exclude specialty recipes. Always check the terms on the deals screen before assuming.

faqs.question: What is the difference between MeatZZa and ExtravaganZZa?
faqs.answer: MeatZZa is meat only — pepperoni, ham, Italian sausage and beef between layers of cheese. ExtravaganZZa takes those same meats and adds onions, green peppers, mushrooms and black olives, so it is the bigger, more mixed version of the same idea.

content:
What Are Domino's Specialty Pizzas?

Specialty pizzas are Domino's pre-built recipes — thirteen named pizzas you order by name rather than assembling yourself. Somebody at Domino's has already decided the topping combination, the cheese blend and the sauce, and the kitchen makes it the same way every time.

That's the whole appeal. You skip the twenty taps of building a pizza and you get combinations most people wouldn't think to put together — an Alfredo base with spinach and feta, or a pizza built on ranch instead of tomato sauce. The trade-off is price: at menu rate they cost noticeably more than a plain cheese pizza, and that's where most people overpay without realising there's a much cheaper way to buy the exact same pizza. We'll get to that.

Usual caveat first: every price here is an example. Domino's stores are individually franchised and set their own prices, so treat these as a ballpark and confirm the real total at checkout.

The Full Specialty Pizza Lineup

Here's every specialty pizza in one table, with what's actually on it and roughly what a large slice costs you in calories.

PizzaWhat's On ItCal / Large Slice
ExtravaganZZaPepperoni, ham, sausage, beef, onions, green peppers, mushrooms, black olives, extra cheese~370
MeatZZaPepperoni, ham, Italian sausage, beef, provolone and mozzarella~350
Cali Chicken Bacon RanchGrilled chicken, bacon, tomatoes, creamy ranch sauce~320
Ultimate PepperoniTwo layers of pepperoni, provolone, Parmesan-Asiago, oregano~330
Spicy Chicken Bacon RanchGrilled chicken, ranch, bacon, jalapeños, buffalo drizzle~320
DeluxePepperoni, Italian sausage, green peppers, mushrooms, onions~290
Philly Cheese SteakSteak, onions, green peppers, mushrooms, provolone and American cheese~290
Honolulu HawaiianHam, bacon, pineapple, roasted red peppers~290
Memphis BBQ ChickenGrilled chicken, honey BBQ sauce, onions, cheddar, provolone~290
Wisconsin 6 CheeseFeta, provolone, cheddar, Parmesan-Asiago, mozzarella, oregano~290
Buffalo ChickenGrilled chicken, hot buffalo sauce, onions, provolone and cheddar~270
Pacific VeggieSpinach, onions, mushrooms, tomatoes, black olives, feta, garlic herb seasoning~230
Spinach & FetaSpinach, feta, onions on a creamy Alfredo base~230

Full calorie numbers for every crust and size are in our Domino's calories and nutrition guide if you want the complete picture.

The Meat Ones

Four pizzas compete for the same customer here, and the differences genuinely matter.

ExtravaganZZa is the maximalist — four meats plus four vegetables plus extra cheese. It's the most food per slice on the entire menu and it eats like a meal rather than a snack. It's also the heaviest at around 370 calories a slice, so three slices is a proper dinner.

MeatZZa is the same idea with the vegetables stripped out: pepperoni, ham, Italian sausage and beef, layered between provolone and mozzarella. If someone at the table picks vegetables off their pizza, this is the one to order.

Ultimate Pepperoni is deceptively simple and probably the safest order in the whole lineup. Two layers of pepperoni with Parmesan-Asiago and oregano — no surprises, and nobody has ever refused a slice of it.

Deluxe sits in the middle: pepperoni and sausage with peppers, mushrooms and onions. It's the classic supreme-style pizza and a good compromise when half the group wants meat and half wants vegetables.

The Chicken Ones

This is where Domino's gets more interesting, because most of these skip tomato sauce entirely.

  • Buffalo Chicken — grilled chicken in hot buffalo sauce with onions, provolone and cheddar. Genuinely spicy, and the lightest specialty with meat on it at about 270 a slice.
  • Memphis BBQ Chicken — honey BBQ sauce instead of tomato, with chicken, onions and cheddar. Sweet rather than hot, and the one children usually go for.
  • Cali Chicken Bacon Ranch — ranch base, grilled chicken, bacon and tomatoes. Rich, creamy, and the closest thing on the menu to comfort food.
  • Spicy Chicken Bacon Ranch — the newest addition, covered properly below.

If you've only ever ordered red-sauce pizzas from Domino's, a ranch-base pizza is the single most surprising thing on the menu. It doesn't taste like pizza-with-ranch-on-it; it tastes like a different dish entirely.

The New One: Spicy Chicken Bacon Ranch

Domino's launched Spicy Chicken Bacon Ranch in late 2025, alongside its "Treat Yo Self" campaign fronted by Retta. It's the newest name on the specialty list and the only one built specifically around heat.

On it: grilled chicken breast, creamy ranch, smoked bacon, jalapeños, provolone and mozzarella, finished with a drizzle of buffalo sauce. It's essentially the Cali Chicken Bacon Ranch with the heat turned up — jalapeños for bite and buffalo on top for tang.

Worth knowing: it launched attached to a $9.99 medium specialty pizza offer, which is the price point Domino's keeps returning to for this category. If you want to try it, check whether that offer is live before paying menu price — our coupons page tracks what's currently running.

The Veggie and Cheese Ones

Three options here, and two of them are the lightest pizzas Domino's makes.

Pacific Veggie is the best non-meat pizza on the menu and it isn't close (see our vegetarian and vegan guide for the full meat-free list) — spinach, onions, mushrooms, tomatoes and black olives with feta and a garlic herb seasoning that does a lot of work. At roughly 230 calories a slice it's also about 140 lighter than the ExtravaganZZa.

Spinach & Feta takes a different route: a creamy Alfredo base instead of tomato, with spinach, feta and onions. It's the more delicate of the two and the better choice if you find loaded veggie pizzas too busy.

Wisconsin 6 Cheese is exactly what it sounds like — feta, provolone, cheddar, Parmesan-Asiago and mozzarella with oregano. No vegetables, no meat, just a lot of cheese. It's the one to order for someone who says they only like cheese pizza but wants something a bit more interesting.

The Two Outliers

Philly Cheese Steak is the least pizza-like pizza on the menu, and that's a compliment. There's no red sauce — it's steak, onions, green peppers and mushrooms under provolone and American cheese. If you're bored of pizza, this is the order that fixes it.

Honolulu Hawaiian is the divisive one, obviously. Ham, bacon, pineapple and roasted red peppers. The bacon is what makes it work — it adds a smokiness that stops the pineapple dominating. You already know which side of this argument you're on.

Specialty Pizza Prices — and the Mistake Most People Make

Here's the part that saves you real money.

OrderSizeExample Price
Specialty pizza, menu priceMedium 12"~$15.99–$16.99
Specialty pizza, menu priceLarge 14"~$16.99–$18.99
Specialty pizza inside a Mix & Match style offerMedium 12"~$9.99 each

Look at the gap between the first row and the last. The same pizza can cost six or seven dollars less depending on how you order it. Domino's regularly runs medium specialty pizzas at around $9.99 when you order two or more qualifying items, and that offer has headlined multiple campaigns.

So the rule is simple: never buy a specialty pizza on its own at menu price if you can help it. If you're ordering anything else — a side, a second pizza, a dessert — build the whole order inside the deal and the specialty drops into the promotional price. Our Mix & Match explainer covers exactly how the multi-item pricing works, and the money-saving playbook covers the rest.

One caveat worth flagging: not every offer includes specialty pizzas. Some any-crust or any-topping promotions specifically exclude specialty recipes. Read the terms on the deals screen rather than assuming — it takes ten seconds and it's the difference between $9.99 and $16.99.

Specialty or Build Your Own?

A fair question, and the answer flips depending on how you're buying.

At menu price, specialty usually wins. Recreating an ExtravaganZZa by hand means paying for eight separate toppings, and per-topping charges add up fast — you'd land well above the specialty price. Our toppings list and prices guide breaks down what each one costs.

Inside a deal, build-your-own usually wins. Most offers are priced around a two-topping pizza, so if you can be happy with pepperoni and mushrooms, you'll pay less than the specialty tier. The exception is when the promotion explicitly includes specialty pizzas, which is when you should absolutely take the free upgrade in complexity.

There's also a middle path people forget: start from a specialty and strip it back. Order an ExtravaganZZa and remove the olives, or a Deluxe without mushrooms. Removals don't normally cost anything, so you get the specialty pricing and a pizza your table will actually finish.

Which One Should You Order?

Quick answers by situation, because that's usually the real question.

  • Feeding a mixed group: Ultimate Pepperoni or Deluxe — nobody objects to either
  • Big appetites: ExtravaganZZa, the most food per slice on the menu
  • Meat only, no vegetables: MeatZZa
  • Something that doesn't taste like usual pizza: Philly Cheese Steak
  • Want heat: Spicy Chicken Bacon Ranch, or Buffalo Chicken for a cleaner burn
  • Watching calories: Pacific Veggie or Spinach & Feta at roughly 230 a slice
  • Kids at the table: Memphis BBQ Chicken — sweet, not spicy
  • Cheese purist who wants more: Wisconsin 6 Cheese

A Few Ordering Tips

Small things that make a real difference to what turns up at your door:

  • Crust changes the pizza more than you'd think. A loaded specialty on Crunchy Thin eats completely differently from the same pizza on Hand Tossed — see our crust types guide.
  • Heavy specialties suit thinner crusts. ExtravaganZZa on a thick base is a lot of pizza; on thin it's balanced.
  • Check whether the deal caps toppings. Some promotions limit topping counts, which can quietly exclude the most loaded specialties.
  • Sizes matter for value. The jump from medium to large is usually a couple of dollars for meaningfully more pizza — our sizes guide has the maths.
  • Don't forget the rest of the order. Sides price better inside the same deal — see the sides menu guide.

The Short Version

Thirteen specialty pizzas, and honestly most people rotate between three of them. Ultimate Pepperoni is the safe one, ExtravaganZZa is the big one, Pacific Veggie is the light one, and Philly Cheese Steak is the one worth trying when you're bored of all of the above. The newest, Spicy Chicken Bacon Ranch, is the one to order if you want heat with your ranch.

But the number that matters most isn't which pizza you pick — it's whether you paid $9.99 or $16.99 for it. Build the order inside a live offer, check the terms cover specialty pizzas, and you'll eat the best pizzas on the menu for close to the price of a plain cheese one. The full lineup with example prices by category is on our Domino's menu with prices page.

faqs.question: What toppings does Domino's have?
faqs.answer: Domino's offers meat toppings including pepperoni, Italian sausage, beef, ham, bacon, Philly steak, grilled chicken and salami, plus vegetables such as mushrooms, onions, green peppers, roasted red peppers, banana peppers, jalapeños, black olives, green olives, pineapple, baby spinach, diced tomatoes and garlic. faqs.question: How much is a topping at Domino's?
faqs.answer: Roughly $1.50 to $3.00 per topping, scaling with pizza size — a small is at the low end, a large at the high end. Stores are individually franchised so the exact charge varies, and it is shown on the running total as you add each one.

faqs.question: How many toppings can you put on a Domino's pizza?
faqs.answer: On a full-price build-your-own you can keep adding toppings, though the price climbs with each one. Promotions are where the limits appear — deals commonly cap you at two, five or seven toppings, and the cap is written into the offer terms.

faqs.question: What sauces does Domino's have for pizza?
faqs.answer: Robust Inspired Tomato Sauce is the standard, with Hearty Marinara, Honey BBQ, Garlic Parmesan, Alfredo and Ranch as alternatives. You can also order light sauce, extra sauce or no sauce at all, and swapping the sauce is normally free.

faqs.question: Does Domino's charge extra for cheese?
faqs.answer: Changing between light and normal cheese is normally free. Extra cheese is a paid upgrade, usually somewhere around $1.50 to $3.00 depending on size, and it adds roughly 40 calories per slice.

faqs.question: Can you get different toppings on each half of a Domino's pizza?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every topping can be applied to the whole pizza, the left half or the right half, which is how you settle an argument between two people without ordering two pizzas. Half toppings are usually charged per side rather than at the full rate.

faqs.question: Which Domino's toppings add the fewest calories?
faqs.answer: Vegetables — mushrooms, onions, peppers, spinach and tomatoes typically add only about 5 to 15 calories per slice. The meats are where it climbs: bacon, sausage and beef are the heaviest, and extra cheese adds roughly 40 a slice on its own.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to build your own pizza or order a specialty?
faqs.answer: At full menu price a specialty pizza usually wins, because paying per topping to recreate it costs more. Inside a deal it reverses — most offers are priced around a two-topping build-your-own, so building your own is cheaper unless the promotion specifically includes specialty pizzas.

faqs.question: Does Domino's have vegetarian toppings?
faqs.answer: Yes, the vegetable range is decent: mushrooms, onions, green and roasted red peppers, banana peppers, jalapeños, black and green olives, pineapple, baby spinach, diced tomatoes and garlic. Note that Domino's prepares everything in a shared kitchen, so cross-contact with meat is possible.

faqs.question: Can you order a Domino's pizza with no sauce or no cheese?
faqs.answer: Yes. Sauce and cheese both have a none option in the builder, alongside light, normal and extra. Ordering no cheese is the usual route for anyone avoiding dairy, though the shared kitchen caveat still applies.

content:
Every Domino's Topping in One Place

The build-your-own screen at Domino's has more going on than most people ever use. There are four separate decisions stacked on top of each other — sauce, cheese, meat, vegetables — and each one has options that quietly change your pizza and your bill.

Most people tap pepperoni and move on. Fair enough. But if you've ever wondered what else is in there, what each topping actually costs, or why your total jumped four dollars between the pizza page and the checkout screen, this is the guide. I'm Dana, I cover ingredients and nutrition for this site, and I'll take the whole builder apart in order.

One thing to say up front: topping availability varies by store, more than people expect. Domino's stores are individually franchised, and some carry items others don't. The lists below are the standard US range — your local store's app is the final word, and so is its pricing.

Meat Toppings

The meats are the expensive part of any pizza and the biggest calorie lever you have.

Meat ToppingWhat It Adds
PepperoniThe default. Salty, crisps at the edges
Italian SausageCrumbled, fennel-forward, heavier than pepperoni
BeefMild and savoury, spreads evenly
HamLean and mild, the pineapple partner
BaconSmoky, and the richest thing on the list
Philly SteakSliced, works best without red sauce
Grilled ChickenThe lightest meat, pairs with ranch and BBQ
SalamiSharper and spicier than pepperoni

A word of warning that will save you money: stacking three or four meats is how a $12 pizza becomes a $20 one. If you want a heavily loaded meat pizza, ordering a MeatZZa or ExtravaganZZa from the specialty pizza lineup is almost always cheaper than building the same thing topping by topping.

Vegetable Toppings

The vegetables are where the value is. They cost the same as the meats but add a fraction of the calories.

VegetableNotes
MushroomsEarthy, releases moisture — go light on thin crust
OnionsSweetens as it bakes, works with everything
Green PeppersThe classic, stays firm
Roasted Red PeppersSweeter and softer than green
Banana PeppersTangy rather than hot
Jalapeño PeppersThe genuine heat option
Black OlivesMild and salty
Green OlivesSharper and brinier
PineappleYou already have an opinion about this
Baby SpinachWilts down, pairs beautifully with feta
Diced TomatoesFresh contrast against heavy cheese
GarlicCheap way to make a plain pizza taste designed

If you're eating vegetarian, the range here is genuinely workable — you can build a proper pizza rather than a compromise, and our vegetarian and vegan guide covers exactly which crusts, sauces and sides qualify. The honest caveat is that Domino's prepares everything in a shared kitchen, so cross-contact with meat is possible. That matters for some people and not others; it's worth knowing either way.

Cheese Options

The base cheese is 100% real mozzarella, and it's more adjustable than people realise:

  • Light, normal or extra — the portion is your choice, and light is a free way to cut roughly 25 calories a slice
  • Extra cheese — a paid upgrade, typically $1.50 to $3.00, adding around 40 calories a slice
  • None — yes, you can order a pizza with no cheese at all
  • Added cheeses — cheddar, feta, provolone and Parmesan-Asiago can be added as separate toppings

The underrated move here is feta on a veggie pizza. It's the ingredient doing most of the work on the Pacific Veggie and Spinach & Feta specialties, and adding it to your own build costs the same as any other topping.

Sauce Options — The Most Overlooked Choice

This is the section most people skip entirely, and it changes the pizza more than any single topping does.

SauceBest With
Robust Inspired TomatoThe default — pepperoni, sausage, beef
Hearty MarinaraMilder than robust, good for kids
Garlic ParmesanChicken, spinach, mushrooms
AlfredoSpinach and feta, or chicken and bacon
Honey BBQChicken, onions, cheddar
RanchChicken, bacon and tomatoes

Swapping the sauce is normally free. That's the whole point — it's the one customisation that costs nothing and completely changes what arrives. If you've only ever had red-sauce pizza from Domino's, ordering the same toppings on a garlic Parmesan or Alfredo base is the cheapest way to make the menu feel new.

You can also set the sauce to light, extra or none, which is worth knowing if you've ever found a pizza soggy in the middle.

How Much Does Each Topping Cost?

Here's the part everyone actually searches for.

Pizza SizePer Extra Topping
Small 10"~$1.50–$2.00
Medium 12"~$2.00–$2.50
Large 14"~$2.00–$3.00

Toppings scale with size, which makes sense — a large pizza needs more of everything. What catches people out is the compounding: four toppings on a large can add $10 or more to a pizza that started at $13. That's how a build-your-own quietly overtakes the price of a specialty.

These are examples, as always on this site. Franchised stores set their own prices, and some charge extra for particular toppings. The running total in the app updates as you tap, so watch it rather than trusting any chart.

Light, Normal, Extra — and Half-and-Half

Two mechanics worth understanding properly, because they're free flexibility most people never touch.

Portion control. Nearly every topping can be ordered light, normal or extra. Extra usually costs more; light usually doesn't. If you like the flavour of jalapeños but not the heat, light is your setting.

Half-and-half. Every topping can go on the whole pizza, the left half or the right half. This is the single most useful feature in the builder and it's badly underused — two people who want different pizzas can share one, and half toppings are typically charged per side rather than at the full rate. For a household where nobody agrees, it beats ordering two mediums. Our family ordering guide covers more of that.

How Many Toppings Can You Add?

On a full-price pizza, you can keep going — the price just keeps climbing. The limits live in the deals, not the menu.

Promotions commonly cap toppings, and the cap is what makes the offer work: a two-topping cap on Mix & Match style deals, five toppings on some carryout specials, seven on the broader "any topping" offers. Some deals also exclude the most loaded specialty recipes for the same reason.

So before you build a six-topping monster inside a deal, read the terms — going one topping over the cap can push the pizza out of the promotional price entirely. Our Mix & Match explainer and the current coupons page cover which offers are running and what they include.

Toppings and Calories

Not all toppings are equal here, and the difference is bigger than most people assume.

  • Vegetables: roughly 5–15 calories a slice. Effectively free.
  • Grilled chicken: around 20–30 a slice. The lightest meat.
  • Ham: similar to chicken, lean and mild.
  • Pepperoni, beef, sausage: roughly 30–50 a slice each.
  • Bacon: the heaviest topping on the list.
  • Extra cheese: around 40 a slice on its own.

The practical version: swapping one meat for one vegetable saves real calories and costs the same money. Pepperoni and mushrooms instead of pepperoni and sausage still tastes like a loaded pizza. Full numbers for every pizza and crust are in our calories and nutrition guide.

Combinations Worth Stealing

A few builds that work better than the sum of their parts:

  • Garlic Parmesan + chicken + spinach + mushrooms — tastes like a restaurant pizza, no red sauce in sight
  • Alfredo + spinach + feta + onions — the Spinach & Feta specialty, built your way
  • BBQ + chicken + onions + cheddar — sweet, smoky, kid-friendly
  • Robust tomato + pepperoni + jalapeño + banana peppers — heat from two directions
  • Robust tomato + sausage + green peppers + onions — the classic supreme, minus the toppings nobody eats
  • Garlic + extra garlic seasoning + light cheese — a cheap pizza that tastes deliberate

A Few Ordering Notes

Small things that change the result:

  • Wet toppings and thin crust don't mix. Mushrooms and fresh tomatoes release water — on Crunchy Thin, order them light. See our crust types guide.
  • Removals don't usually save money. Taking a topping off a specialty rarely lowers the price, but it does make the pizza better if nobody eats olives.
  • Build inside the deal, not beside it. Adding toppings to a promotional pizza is normally cheaper than starting from menu price.
  • Size changes topping cost. If you're adding four toppings, check whether a medium inside a deal beats a large at menu price — our sizes guide has the maths.

The Short Version

Eight meats, a dozen vegetables, four extra cheeses and six sauces — that's a lot more pizza than most people ever order. The sauce swap is free and changes everything. Vegetables cost the same as meat and add almost nothing to the calorie count. Half-and-half solves arguments. And every topping past the second or third is where the bill quietly runs away from you.

Build it inside a live offer, watch the running total, and you'll get a better pizza than the one you keep ordering out of habit. Example prices for the whole menu are on our Domino's menu with prices page — and the checkout screen is still the only number that counts.

title: Domino's Coupons & Promo Codes (2026): Every Deal Explained
excerpt: Skip the coupon-hunting rabbit hole. Here's how Domino's deals really work in 2026, which ones are worth it, and how to squeeze them together.
author: amna-sadam
imageAlt: A Domino's order with a coupon code overlay

faqs.question: Where do I enter a Domino's promo code?
faqs.answer: On the official Domino's app or website, promo codes are entered in the coupon or deals section at checkout. Many deals apply automatically when you add qualifying items to your cart.

faqs.question: Does Domino's have a coupon for a free pizza?
faqs.answer: The most reliable way to get a free pizza is through Domino's Rewards, which awards a free medium two-topping pizza once you accumulate enough points. Occasional promotions also offer free items with a qualifying purchase.

faqs.question: Are Domino's online coupons better than in-store?
faqs.answer: Online and app-based deals are usually the best, since digital pricing tends to reflect the current national promotions. Carryout deals in particular are often exclusive to online ordering.

faqs.question: How do I get the cheapest Domino's order?
faqs.answer: Build your order inside Mix & Match or $6.99 Each, choose carryout to skip the delivery fee, order in the app, and stay signed into Domino's Rewards. Stacking those four routinely cuts 25–40% off.

faqs.question: Can I use more than one coupon at a time?
faqs.answer: Generally no — you can't stack two coupons on the same items. But you can combine a value deal with carryout and rewards, which saves you three different ways without needing two codes.

faqs.question: Do Domino's coupon codes expire?
faqs.answer: Yes, limited-time codes expire and the standing deals rotate. Always confirm the offer is live in the official app before you rely on it.

faqs.question: Are these coupon codes guaranteed to work?
faqs.answer: No. The offers here are examples for guidance, not guaranteed codes. Verify the live deal on the official Domino's app, and never trust a third party promising a guaranteed free-pizza code.

content:
Stop Hunting for Random Codes

Here's a confession from someone who's spent way too many hours on this stuff: most of the Domino's promo codes floating around the internet are junk. Expired, fake, or region-locked to somewhere that isn't where you live. You paste them in, hit apply, and get that little red error message that quietly ruins your evening. The truth is, Domino's doesn't really run on secret codes. It runs on a handful of recurring deals, and once you understand those, you'll never need to Google a coupon again. Promise.

So instead of sending you on a scavenger hunt across a dozen sketchy coupon sites, let me walk you through the deals that actually matter — what each one does, who it's built for, and the little catches nobody mentions. The live, copyable versions sit on our coupons page whenever you're ready to order.

Every Domino's Deal at a Glance

Before we go one by one, here's the whole landscape in a single view. Bookmark this table and you've basically got the strategy memorized.

DealWhat It DoesBest For
Mix & Match2+ items at a fixed price eachEveryday orders, any size
$6.99 Each3+ items at a low flat priceFamilies, parties, big groups
50% Off Menu PizzasHalf off full-price pizzasA specialty not in the deal
Carryout SpecialDiscount for pickup ordersAnyone who can drive over
Emergency Pizza & wild cardsFree pizza / limited promosRewards members

Mix & Match — The One You'll Use Most

This is the workhorse, the deal you'll come back to again and again. Pick two or more items, pay a fixed price for each, done. Pizzas, sides, pasta, chicken — they nearly all play. What makes it special, and what most people don't realize, is that specialty pizzas usually count too. So you're not stuck ordering a plain cheese just to save money. You can load up a fully dressed specialty and pay the same per-item rate. I broke the whole thing down in the Mix & Match guide, but honestly, this one deal covers the majority of orders you'll ever place.

Who It's Best For

Just about everyone, which is exactly why it's the default. Solo diners pair a pizza with a side. Couples grab two mediums. Families mix a couple of pizzas with bread and a dessert. If you only ever learn one Domino's deal in your life, make it this one.

$6.99 Each When You Buy Three

Feeding a crowd? Bump up to three or more items and each one drops to a low flat price. It quietly beats Mix & Match once you're ordering that much food anyway, so it's always worth comparing the two right there at checkout. Think game night, think a house full of teenagers who somehow eat their weight in pizza, think the office lunch nobody planned properly until 11am. This is the deal that shines the moment the order gets big.

Half Off Menu-Price Pizzas

Every so often Domino's knocks 50% off pizzas ordered at regular menu price. Simple, no gymnastics required, and it's genuinely handy when you want a specialty pie that isn't in this week's Mix & Match rotation. The catch? It's a limited-time thing that comes and goes without much warning. When you spot it in the app, grab it, because it might be gone next week and you'll be kicking yourself.

Carryout Is the Quiet Champion

Want to know the cheapest trick that nobody thinks is a trick? Just go pick it up. Carryout skips the delivery fee entirely — that's four to six bucks back in your pocket before you even factor in a tip — and Domino's regularly runs carryout-only large-pizza specials that undercut everything else on the menu. If your couch can survive a ten-minute round trip, your wallet will genuinely thank you. I lean on this one constantly, and it's the single easiest saving on this whole list.

The Limited-Time Wild Cards

Then there are the headline stunts — things like Emergency Pizza, where rewards members bank a free pie to redeem on a rough day later. These promotions are fun, occasionally very generous, and completely unpredictable. My rule is simple: always check the deals tab in the app before you order, because every so often the wild card beats every standing deal by a mile, and you'd hate to miss it by thirty seconds of impatience. Holidays, big game weekends, and back-to-school season tend to bring the best of these out, so keep an eye out around then.

Which Deal Should You Use? Quick Guide

Deals only help if you pick the right one for your situation. Here's the cheat sheet.

Your SituationReach For
Just you, one dinnerMix & Match (2 items)
Couple or small orderMix & Match
Family or 3+ items$6.99 Each
Want one specialty pizza50% Off Menu, if live
Can pick it upCarryout Special, always

What About Student and Military Discounts?

People ask about these a lot. Domino's discounts here vary widely by location and aren't a guaranteed national thing, so the honest answer is to check with your local store or the app rather than counting on a fixed percentage. Often the standing value deals — Mix & Match and carryout — end up beating a small percentage discount anyway, so don't overlook the everyday deals while hunting for a special one.

How to Enter a Code (and Why Most Apply Themselves)

People ask me where the promo code box lives, and here's the honest answer — you often won't need it at all. Most of Domino's best deals apply automatically the moment you add qualifying items to your cart. When there is a code, it goes in the coupon or deals section at checkout in the app or on the website. If a deal isn't showing up, back out and check that your items actually qualify. Nine times out of ten, that's the entire fix.

Can You Stack Everything? Sort Of.

Let's kill the myth right now: you generally can't slap two coupons on the same pizza. Sorry, that dream isn't real. But you can absolutely layer strategy, which is almost as good. Order through a value deal, choose carryout to kill the delivery fee, and stay logged into Domino's Rewards so every single order quietly builds toward a freebie in the background. Do all three at once and you're saving three different ways without ever needing a magic code. The full math lives in the money-saving guide, and the whole menu with prices is worth a look before you build your cart.

How to Spot a Fake Coupon

One last warning, because it matters. If a code promises something absurd — a totally free large pizza with no purchase, say — it's almost certainly fake or a data-harvesting trap. Real Domino's deals live in the official app and on the official site, full stop. Anything asking you to fill out surveys or hand over personal details to 'unlock' a coupon is a red flag. Stick to official sources and you'll never get burned.

A Quick Reality Check

Deals shift constantly and vary store to store — what's live in one city might not exist two states over. I keep this page current, but we're an independent, unofficial guide, not Domino's HQ. Confirm any offer in the official app before you count on it, and never, ever trust a stranger online promising a guaranteed free-pizza code. If it sounds too good to be true, it almost always is. Order smart, verify at checkout, and enjoy the pizza — that's the whole point.

title: Domino's Calories & Nutrition Guide (2026): Every Slice, Size & Side
excerpt: How many calories are in a slice of Domino's pizza? A plain-English breakdown of calories by size, crust, specialty pizza, wings, sides, pasta and dessert — plus the lowest-calorie way to order.

faqs.question: How many calories are in a slice of Domino's pizza?
faqs.answer: Most Domino's slices land between about 150 and 380 calories. A large Hand Tossed cheese slice is roughly 270 calories, a large pepperoni slice about 300, and a medium Crunchy Thin cheese slice can be as low as 150. Loaded specialty pizzas like the ExtravaganZZa push past 350 per slice.

faqs.question: How many calories are in a whole large Domino's pizza?
faqs.answer: A large 14-inch Hand Tossed cheese pizza is roughly 2,160 calories across its 8 slices, and the pepperoni version is around 2,400. Switching that same large to Crunchy Thin drops it to roughly 1,600 calories.

faqs.question: How many calories are in a medium Domino's pizza?
faqs.answer: A medium 12-inch Hand Tossed cheese pizza is about 1,720 calories in total, or roughly 215 per slice across 8 slices. A medium pepperoni comes in around 1,920 calories.

faqs.question: Which Domino's pizza has the fewest calories?
faqs.answer: A Crunchy Thin cheese or veggie pizza is the lightest thing on the pizza menu — around 150 calories per medium slice. Order it with light cheese and vegetable toppings and you have the lowest-calorie pizza Domino's makes.

faqs.question: Is Domino's thin crust lower in calories?
faqs.answer: Yes, noticeably. Crunchy Thin uses far less dough, so it typically saves 60 to 90 calories per slice compared with Hand Tossed. Over a whole pizza that is often 500 calories or more.

faqs.question: How many calories are in Domino's Stuffed Cheesy Bread?
faqs.answer: Roughly 260 calories for two pieces of the plain version, so a full 8-piece order lands north of 1,000 calories. The Pepperoni and Spinach & Feta versions are slightly higher per piece.

faqs.question: How many calories are in Domino's boneless chicken and wings?
faqs.answer: Boneless chicken is about 50 calories per piece, so an 8-piece order is roughly 400. Plain bone-in wings are around 55 each, and sauced versions such as Hot Buffalo or Sweet BBQ run 65 to 70 per wing before dipping sauce.

faqs.question: Does Domino's show calories when you order?
faqs.answer: Yes. Domino's publishes a nutrition guide and a Cal-O-Meter tool that recalculates calories as you build a pizza, and US stores display calorie information at the point of ordering. That live tool is always more accurate than any third-party chart, including this one.

faqs.question: How many calories are in Domino's Chocolate Lava Crunch Cake?
faqs.answer: About 350 calories per cake. They are sold in twos, so an order is roughly 700 calories if you eat both.

faqs.question: Can you eat Domino's while watching your calories?
faqs.answer: Comfortably, yes — it just takes ordering on purpose. Two slices of medium Crunchy Thin veggie with light cheese is around 300 calories, which fits most days. The calories pile up from the extras: dips, garlic bread, soda and a third or fourth slice.

content:
How Many Calories Are in a Slice of Domino's Pizza?

Short answer first, because that's what you came for: a slice of Domino's pizza runs roughly 150 to 380 calories, depending on size, crust and toppings. A large Hand Tossed cheese slice sits around 270. Add pepperoni and you're near 300. Go Crunchy Thin on a medium and you can drop to about 150 a slice.

That spread is huge — more than double from one end to the other — and it's entirely under your control at checkout. So let me lay out the whole menu, category by category, so you can see exactly where the calories live and where they don't. I'm Dana, I write the nutrition side of this guide, and I'm not here to talk you out of ordering pizza. I'm here to help you order the pizza you actually want without being blindsided by the number.

One honest note before the tables: these are approximate figures for guidance, gathered from published nutrition data. Real numbers move with portioning, toppings and store. When you need precision, build your order in the Domino's app and read the live calorie count — nothing beats that.

Domino's Calories Per Slice by Size

This is the table most people are looking for. Hand Tossed is the default crust, so it's the fair baseline for comparing sizes.

SizeSlicesCheese (per slice)Pepperoni (per slice)
Small — 10"6~200 cal~230 cal
Medium — 12"8~215 cal~240 cal
Large — 14"8~270 cal~300 cal

Notice the trap in that table: a large slice isn't a small slice. People assume "two slices" means the same thing everywhere, but two large Hand Tossed pepperoni slices (~600 calories) is nearly the same as three small cheese slices. If you're counting, count the size too, not just the slice. Our Domino's pizza sizes guide breaks down the diameters and how many each one actually feeds.

Whole Pizza Calories

And here's the total for the box, for anyone splitting a pizza and doing the maths in their head.

PizzaCrustWhole Pizza
Small cheeseHand Tossed~1,200 cal
Small pepperoniHand Tossed~1,380 cal
Medium cheeseHand Tossed~1,720 cal

Large cheeseHand Tossed~2,160 cal
Large pepperoniHand Tossed~2,400 cal
Medium cheeseCrunchy Thin~1,200 cal
Large cheeseCrunchy Thin~1,600 cal
Large pepperoniCrunchy Thin~2,000 cal

Look at the last three rows against the ones above them. Same size, same toppings, same price — about 500 fewer calories per large pizza just from the crust choice. That's the single easiest swap on this entire page.

Domino's Calories by Crust

Crust is where the dough is, and dough is where the calories are. Here's every crust compared like-for-like: cheese pizza, per slice.

CrustSize ComparedPer SliceVerdict
Crunchy ThinMedium~150 calLightest by a mile

Hand TossedMedium~215 calThe default baseline

Parmesan Stuffed CrustMediumHighest — check in appCheese baked into the rim

A word on the newest one: Parmesan Stuffed Crust is Domino's first stuffed crust, and it puts mozzarella inside the rim with Parmesan and garlic seasoning on top. There's no way around it — melted cheese baked into the edge is extra calories on every slice, and it's the one crust I'd genuinely check in the app before ordering rather than estimating. It's a treat crust, and that's fine, as long as you order it knowing that — our Parmesan Stuffed Crust guide covers the price, sizes and whether it's worth the upcharge. If you want the taste and texture rundown on the rest, read our Domino's crust types guide, and the gluten-free crust guide if wheat is the issue rather than calories.

Specialty Pizza Calories

Specialty pizzas come pre-loaded, and the toppings do real damage. These are large Hand Tossed slices, so compare them against that ~270 cheese baseline.

The gap between Pacific Veggie and ExtravaganZZa is about 140 calories a slice. Our specialty pizzas guide lists what's on every one of them. Eat three slices and that's a 420-calorie difference from one menu decision. Veggie-forward specialties are the quiet win here — they still taste like a proper loaded pizza, they just don't stack meat on meat on cheese.

Wings, Chicken & Bread Sides

Here's where most orders quietly double. The pizza gets all the attention while the sides sail through unexamined.

SideServingCalories
Boneless ChickenPer piece / 8 pc~50 / ~400 cal
Plain WingsPer piece / 8 pc~55 / ~440 cal
Hot Buffalo Wings8 pieces~520 cal

Read that last row twice. A full order of Stuffed Cheesy Bread can out-calorie half a large pizza. It's delicious and I'm not banning it — but it is a main course pretending to be a side, and it should replace a couple of slices rather than sit next to them. Prices and portions for the chicken range are in our chicken and wings menu guide.

Pasta & Bread Bowls

Pasta looks like the sensible choice next to pizza. It isn't always — and the bread bowl is the reason.

PastaDishBread Bowl
Pasta Primavera~530–550 calVaries
Chicken Alfredo~620 cal~690 cal
Italian Sausage Marinara~690 cal~730 cal
Chicken Carbonara~690 calVaries

A correction worth flagging, because this page previously said otherwise: the bread bowl adds far less than people assume. Published figures put Chicken Alfredo at around 620 in a dish and 690 in a bread bowl, and Italian Sausage Marinara at roughly 690 and 730 — a step of 40 to 70 calories rather than the several hundred you would expect from a loaf of bread. The likely explanation is that the pasta portion inside a bowl is smaller than the dish portion, and sources disagree on the bowl entries more than on the dish ones. If the number matters to you, build it in the app. Prices for the whole non-pizza range are in our Domino's sides menu guide.

Desserts & Dipping Sauces

Small items, sneaky numbers. Dips especially — nobody logs a dipping cup.

ItemServingCalories
Chocolate Lava Crunch Cake1 cake~350 cal
Cinnamon Bread Twists2 pieces~250 cal
Marbled Cookie Brownie1 piece~200 cal
